page: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is a burstable performance instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton processors with Neoverse-N1 cores running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, this server features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography enabled. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals average performance across several standard workloads, alongside notable weaknesses in specific compute tasks. The instance achieves average results in stress-ng single-core (1519.68) and multi-core (12133.02) CPU tests, as well as average scores in Geekbench multi-core (5322.0) and software compilation (8387.0). Memory bandwidth is robust, measuring 472.63 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 114.09 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-threaded performance is a bottleneck, with poor ratings in Geekbench single-core (907.0) and bzip3 decompression (7.11 GB/sec), and weak ratings in Passmark CPU (5230.38) and memory scores (1613.52). LLM inference speeds are also low, generating only 6.73 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t4g.2xlarge offers a budget-friendly entry point for multi-core ARM64 development and testing due to its burstable CPU allocation model. The primary tradeoff is the burstable CPU credit system, which makes it unsuitable for sustained high-CPU workloads, combined with its weak single-threaded performance and lack of local NVMe storage. It is appropriate for workloads with fluctuating CPU demands, such as static web serving (which achieved an average throughput of 9.19 GB/sec), Redis caching (9.35 million operations/sec), database operations, and general-purpose microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.2xlarge is a burstable, general-purpose instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 32.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core) and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmarks show average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.02 and static web serving throughput of 9.19 GB/sec, though single-threaded performance remains weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 907.0. Qualitatively, this instance provides a cost-effective option for ARM64 development and bursty workloads. It is suited for static web serving, Redis caching, database operations, and microservices that do not require sustained, continuous CPU utilization.
